name: Bahamas — bonefish flats
primaryFactor: Tide stage decides when fish are on a flat; wind direction decides which flat is fishable at all.

waters.name: Hard sand flat
waters.notes: Wade-able, best on a pushing tide. Fish are visible at distance in good light.

waters.name: Turtle grass flat
waters.notes: Fish are harder to see and flies hang up. Lighter eyes or a weed guard.

waters.name: Mangrove edge
waters.notes: Holds fish on high water; they push in to feed and come back out on the drop.

waters.name: Creek mouth
waters.notes: Ambush point on a falling tide — fish funnel out.

notes: Resident bonefish year-round; the calendar question is weather, not presence. Spring is the settled-weather window. Winter cold fronts are the real risk to a booked week.
sources: Tide station 9710441 = Settlement Point, Grand Bahama (26.71, -79.00). Station verified against the NOAA CO-OPS metadata API, 2026-09-14.
Flat descriptions and the spring-window claim are still unverified.

species.label: Bonefish
species.season: year-round, best Oct–May; bigger fish than Belize, wading flats
species.leader: 10-12 ft, 10-12 lb (16 lb on Andros for big fish)

species.label: Permit
species.season: spring–summer, Andros west side, Abaco

species.label: Barracuda
species.season: winter on flats

name: North Carolina coast
primaryFactor: Bait, then wind. The fall albacore fishery follows glass minnows and finger mullet out of the Pamlico, Albemarle and Core sounds and stacks them at the inlets.

waters.name: Barden's Inlet, Cape Lookout
waters.notes: The albie inlet. Bait funnels through it out of the sounds; fish the current seams.

waters.name: Inlet
waters.notes: Albie water in fall. Current seams stack bait.

waters.name: Marsh edge
waters.notes: Smooth cordgrass, not mangrove — redfish push in on a flooding tide and back out as it drops.

notes: Fall false albacore run is the marquee event; redfish are the year-round backstop.
sources: Tide station 8656483 = Beaufort, Duke Marine Lab, NC (34.717, -76.671). Station verified against the NOAA CO-OPS metadata API, 2026-09-14.

species.label: Redfish (red drum)

species.season: Oct–Nov at Cape Lookout

species.label: Striped bass
species.season: Nov–Feb Roanoke/OBX, spring Roanoke River run

species.label: Bluefish

name: Belize
primaryFactor: Wind and cold fronts through March; tide on the flats.

waters.name: Lagoon and river mouth
waters.notes: Resident juvenile tarpon hold here year-round.

notes: Resident juvenile tarpon are available year-round. Migratory adults are a late-spring-into-summer proposition, so an early-spring week is really a permit and bonefish trip with tarpon as a bonus.

notes: Bonefish are typically smaller and in larger schools than the Bahamas — more shots, smaller fish, and they spook as a group.

name: Idaho — South Fork country
primaryFactor: Flow. A big change in cfs resets where fish sit and what they eat before any hatch does.

waters.name: Seam
waters.notes: Where the 19" cutthroat came from — 3 ft, moderate.

notes: Cutthroat and rainbows; fall is the settled window.
sources: Gauge 13037500 = Snake River near Heise, ID — the standard South Fork gauge. Station verified against the USGS site service, 2026-09-14. (My earlier label said 'near Irwin'; Irwin is a different station, 13032500.)

species.label: Rainbow trout

name: North Carolina mountains
primaryFactor: Water temperature and clarity. Freestone streams swing fast after rain.
notes: Small water, short casts, fish that see pressure. Midges and BWOs carry the cold months.
sources: Gauge 03441000 = Davidson River near Brevard, NC (35.273, -82.706). Station verified against the USGS site service, 2026-09-14.
